subject_group: 9.4.4 External visibility and transmitted visual indications

versions.text:
Standard: Enhanced vision system and EVFS imagery are free of interference, distortion, and glare that would adversely affect pilot’s performance and workload. For flight-critical functions, the imagery does not provide the pilot with misleading information regarding detection, accurate identification and avoidance of terrain, obstacles, and other flight hazards. Imagery displayed on the HUD or equivalent display conforms to the real-world and is appropriate for the system’s intended function, accounting for possible air vehicle attitudes, turbulence, and wind effects. If PFD information is displayed, it is accurate, and the horizon is conformal and aligned with the imagery. For other EVS characteristics refer to FAA AC 20-167A Airworthiness Approval of Enhanced Vision System, Synthetic Vision System, Combined Vision System, and Enhanced Flight Vision System Equipment, sections - EVS or SVS (or CVS when EVS and SVS combined) – General and EVS Specific Requirements. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Demonstration.
(1) Demonstrate that the EVS image, as installed in the air vehicle, is free of interference, distortion, and glare that would adversely affect pilot performance and workload (e.g., reduced ability to accomplish tasks or degraded workload scores) for all intended flight conditions.
(2) Demonstrate that the imagery allows the pilot to detect, identify, and avoid terrain, obstacles, and other flight hazards for all intended flight conditions.
(3) Demonstrate that the imagery is conformal if the imagery is shown on a HUD or equivalent display for all intended flight conditions.
(4) Demonstrate that the PFD information agrees with other flight displays and that the horizon is aligned with the imagery and conformal for all intended flight conditions. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
(5) Demonstrate in flight that the EVS image is free of interference, distortion, and glare that would adversely affect pilot performance and workload.
(6) Demonstrate in flight that the imagery accurately detects, identifies and allows for the avoidance of terrain, obstacles, and other flight hazards.
(7) Demonstrate in flight that the imagery is conformal if the imagery is shown on a HUD or equivalent display.
(8) Demonstrate in flight that the PFD information is accurate, and that the horizon is conformal and aligned with the imagery.
